selection_rationale: cnd-01 directly targets the key identified gap—integrating LLM-generated configs with deterministic verifiers—and received a "pass" reviewer verdict while balancing novelty, falsifiability, and compute feasibility; it yields a clear, paired experimental design suited to CNSM's operational-reliability focus.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier expressivity and coverage may miss operational semantics causing false negatives (how to bound claims to verifier-covered properties).
Representativeness and operational realism of the curated intent-to-configuration task set (do 120 tasks capture real NetOps difficulty distribution?).
Generalisability across LLMs, API nondeterminism, and vendor changes (to what extent results transfer beyond the tested model versions).
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Pin exact LLM model identifiers, API versions, and deterministic generation settings (temperature, top_p, seeds) and record them in the preregistration.
Specify verifier tool, exact version, supported properties, and documented limitations (e.g., Batfish version and precise property coverage).
Provide explicit task sourcing protocol: provenance, inclusion/exclusion rules, complexity-labeling criteria, example tasks, and held-out/seed rules.
Add a formal sample-size/power calculation for the primary paired binary outcome and justify or adjust the planned 120-task sample accordingly.
Define and freeze retry policy, prompt templates and full prompt text, random-seed control, logging/hashing requirements, and unit/integration tests for the repair-loop orchestration.
